The short version

Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp make money by standing between the homeowner and your business. You pay per lead, per contact or per click, and the same homeowner is often shown other pros too. A Google Business Profile is free and essential, but it shows competitors right beside you. Enoma is a page that's only about you, for one flat monthly price, and the call goes straight to you.

That doesn't mean you should drop everything else. It means you should know what each one is for.

When each one makes sense

Angi and Thumbtack

Useful when you're new, your calendar has gaps, and you can answer every lead within minutes. Speed decides most marketplace jobs. Track cost per booked job, not cost per lead, and cut back as your own calls grow.

Yelp

Keep your free page claimed and accurate: Yelp listings show up in Google and AI assistants read them. Paid Yelp ads work in some cities and trades and not in others. Test with a small budget and a hard monthly cap.

Nextdoor

Good for neighbor recommendations and word of mouth. It's a feed, not a search engine, so it won't help much when someone Googles "[your service] near me".

Google Business Profile

Non-negotiable. It's free and it's where most local searches start. Fill in every field, pick the right primary category, list your towns and ask every customer for a review.

Enoma

For owners who want calls they don't share and don't have time to build a website. Your page names your services and towns so Google and AI assistants understand what you do, your Business Profile links to it, and every call and quote request goes straight to you.

Want to see yours? We build it from your Google listing in about 30 seconds, and you see it live before you pay anything. See your page.

A sensible setup for most trades

  1. A complete, verified Google Business Profile.
  2. A page of your own that your profile links to.
  3. A review request sent after every job.
  4. Marketplaces only as a top-up, judged on cost per booked job.

Common questions

Enoma vs Angi, Thumbtack, Yelp and Google, side by side: common questions

Is Enoma a lead marketplace like Angi or Thumbtack?

No. Enoma doesn't sell leads. It builds a one-page website for your business, and every call or quote request from that page goes only to you. You pay $19.99 a month after a free first month, with no per-lead fees.

Should I cancel Angi or Thumbtack if I get an Enoma page?

Not right away. Keep anything that books jobs profitably, track cost per booked job for each source for a month or two, and cut the ones that cost the most per job as calls from your own page and Google listing grow.

Do I still need a Google Business Profile if I have an Enoma page?

Yes. Your Google Business Profile is where most local searches start. Link it to your Enoma page so Google and customers find the same services, towns and phone number in both places.

Why does cost per booked job matter more than cost per lead?

Because you can pay for a lead and never win the job, especially when the same homeowner hears from several pros. Dividing what you spent by the jobs you actually booked shows what each customer really cost.

What does Enoma cost?

Your first month is free, with no credit card. After that it's $19.99 a month to keep your page live, and that includes personal support. No contract; cancel anytime.
